key_insight: EPPC-CARE improved automated annotation of communication behaviors by sequentially identifying source text, a broad category, and a specific subcategory.
clinical_relevance: Linking communication labels to supporting message text could help researchers review annotations and study patient-provider communication at scale.
method: Produces annotation triplets: text span, communication code, and subcode.
Identifies triplet components sequentially using a staged hierarchical framework.
Evaluated across six open-weight LLMs against supervised fine-tuning and communication-focused models.
evidence_signal: Using 5,516 reference annotations from 867 messages, EPPC-CARE improved Triplet F1 over EPPC-OASIS by 2.90 percentage points on average, reached a best score of 64.4%, and showed agreement with the reference standard comparable to a human expert on 100 messages.
watch_item: The reported annotation performance does not establish improved patient outcomes, and broader deployment would require validation and human review.
paper_title: EPPC-CARE: Staged Hierarchical Annotation of Communication Behaviors in Secure Patient-Provider Messages
